payload.title: kernel-dead-wire reports unrouted nested verbs by counting them per group (fewer than two stay silent), so a live fall-through verb is reported dead with a false message when a sibling is dead, a lone dead verb is hidden, and the 19 silent verbs of the real CLI include ones routed by a form the route regexes never read
evidence: tools/aria-adapters/kernel-dead-wire-adapter.ts:282-295 (a nested verb is skipped when fewer than two unrouted verbs share its dest)
tools/aria-adapters/kernel-dead-wire-adapter.ts:296-307 (every reported verb gets the message that no branch dispatches it)
tools/aria-adapters/kernel-dead-wire-adapter.ts:105-107 (a route is read only as args.<dest> == literal or args.<dest> in a tuple or set literal)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/cli.py:3876-3877 (cycle run is dispatched by getattr(args, "cycle_command", None) == "run", a form no route regex reads)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/cli.py:7538-7547 (security zap validate runs with no reference to args.security_zap_command)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/cli.py:7560-7565 (security regression list has the same shape)
tools/aria-adapters/kernel-dead-wire-adapter.test.ts:85-122 (the fixture holds two dead siblings only: no live fall-through sibling, no lone dead verb, no getattr route)
payload.rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach: a detector must model the thing it judges; a count that stands in for dispatch hides different causes behind one number
payload.notes: Reproduced by reading the filter: in a group with one routed verb, one dead verb and one live verb reached by falling off the end of the branches, both unrouted verbs are reported and the live one is told that no branch dispatches it. A group whose only unrouted verb is dead is silent. Re-running the adapter's regexes over cli.py at this revision gives exactly 19 unrouted verbs, one per group; among them cycle run is routed through getattr, and security zap validate and security regression list are single-verb groups the handler never tests, so three different causes sit behind one silence rule. Adding a second unrouted verb to the cycle group would also report cycle run, the verb the nightly cycle invokes. Close condition: Model dispatch instead of counting: read the getattr(args, "<dest>", ...) == form, treat a group's handler-less single verb through an explicit declaration, and word the finding so it does not claim 'dead' for a possible fall-through; closed when kernel-dead-wire-adapter.test.ts has synthetic cases for a lone dead verb, a live fall-through sibling and a getattr-routed verb, and the 19 silent production verbs are each explained or reported. Plan row: DET detector program (landing batch 2b). Verified at head b2259fe03f of open pull request #2151; the cited code is not on main until that pull request merges.
